clue.text: New trench coat for expert in senior position

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters of the two words are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A fresh trench coat is bought for a senior specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective for the coat but it signals rearranging TRENCH COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A technocrat is a technical specialist given power or high office in government or industry.

clue.text: Man, maybe, in passageway, losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the word for passageway is dropped

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: Someone named Man, perhaps, standing in a corridor and losing his composure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea between Britain and Ireland; 'maybe' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island, so Man, maybe, defines the word by example.

clue.text: Sauce boat raised

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
up means raised, lifted

explanation.surface: A gravy boat being lifted from the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce boat' reads as one item of tableware, but the definition stops at 'Sauce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato ketchup is a common bottled sauce.

clue.text: Feathers in fruit tree, silver and blue at the end

parts.note: a plum is a fruit tree
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: at the end means only the last letter of blue is used

explanation.surface: Bird feathers caught in a fruit tree, with silver and blue tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is the whole covering of feathers on a bird.

clue.text: Turn Indian sign

definitions.meaning: a turn of duty or work is a ..., as in a ... at the wheel
an old American idiom for a hex or curse put on someone, a magic charm

explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a period of duty and an Indian sign is a jinx; the answer covers a stint and an enchantment.

clue.text: Grumpy note, last from casualty

parts.note: a crotchet is a musical note, a quarter note

indicators.note: last from means the final letter of casualty is taken

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered message left by the last patient out of A&E.
explanation.walkthrough: A crotchet is the British name for a quarter note in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Crotchety is a synonym for irritable or bad-tempered.

clue.text: Book on facing one's counterparts

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: opposite means facing
Numbers is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A book on how to face up to your opposite number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' is the biblical book of Numbers; 'on' puts it after the word for facing.
explanation.definitionFit: Your opposite numbers are the people holding the equivalent role on the other side, your counterparts.

clue.text: Be shrewd at work noting who gets confused

indicators.note: being confused means the words at work noting who are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone noting at work who becomes muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To know a thing or two is an idiom for being experienced and astute.

clue.text: A provider of Dutch courage? Ten in bar, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective, means dubious, so the letters of ten in bar I are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A drinker suspects that ten people in the pub have been drinking for courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch courage' is confidence gained from alcohol, and 'I suspect' reads as the speaker's guess but 'suspect' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriant is an intoxicating drink, which supplies the false bravery called Dutch courage.

clue.text: Force, extremely tough, after support on course

indicators.note: after places the piece from tough behind the golf support

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball on the course

indicators.note: extremely means the first and last letters of tough are taken

explanation.surface: A golfer forcing a tough shot after teeing up on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth means effective force or power, as in a law with teeth.

clue.text: Book English camps as well

parts.note: camps are opposing factions, sides

explanation.surface: Booking English holiday camps too.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides is an adverb meaning in addition, also.

clue.text: Vegetable that's given away in French inn

indicators.note: given away means the letters of the word in are surrendered from the vegetable

parts.note: aubergine is the British name for eggplant

explanation.surface: Vegetables being handed out free at a French inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but it is the letters removed from AUBERGINE.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn or country hotel.

clue.text: Get listener's attention, finally

parts.note: the ear is the organ of listening, so a listener

indicators.note: finally means just the last letter of attention is used

explanation.surface: At last catching the audience's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to get or gain, as in earning a reward.

clue.text: Comp, kind crossword compiler put together

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a setter is the person who compiles a crossword

explanation.surface: Assembling a crossword competition with a kindly compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comp' looks like short for competition, but it is printers' slang for compositor.
explanation.definitionFit: Comp is short for compositor, the printing worker who sets type.

clue.text: Make assessment is what a shoplifter might do

definitions.meaning: to review a situation and weigh it up
a shoplifter literally removes items of a shop's goods

explanation.definitionFit: Taking stock means appraising a situation; literally, a shop thief takes the store's merchandise.

clue.text: Copper to restrain attractive girl

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to tie is to bind or restrain

explanation.surface: A policeman restraining a pretty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer but gives the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutie is an informal word for an attractive person, especially a girl.

clue.text: Without restrictions, her brood lands abroad

indicators.note: abroad in its older sense of widely scattered, so the letters of her brood lands are spread about

explanation.surface: A mother bird's brood flies off overseas, unrestricted.
explanation.definitionFit: No holds barred, from wrestling, is an idiom for with no rules or limits.

clue.text: Imitation issue published by spiteful woman

parts.note: copy is published matter, the text of an issue
a cat is slang for a spiteful, malicious woman

explanation.surface: A fake edition put out by a catty woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Copycat used before a noun means imitative, as in a copycat crime.

clue.text: A record cut without second wind instrument

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: without means the letter for second is left out of the word for cut

parts.note: shorn means cut, as of hair or wool

explanation.surface: A recording trimmed with the second wind section removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphorn is a long wooden horn blown in the Alps, a wind instrument.

clue.text: Account of soldiers in country close to defeat

indicators.note: in means the soldiers are put inside the country plus that letter

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of defeat

parts.note: men is a common term for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A report of troops in a nation on the brink of defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is an account, as in a bank statement or witness's statement.

clue.text: On in centre of graveyards: a mournful song

indicators.note: in means the cricket word goes inside the middle letters
centre of means the middle two letters of graveyards

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Moving through the middle of graveyards, a sad song.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a lament, a poem or song of mourning for the dead.

clue.text: Embarrassed, being powerless to secure compensation

indicators.note: to secure means the word for powerless holds the compensation inside

parts.note: unable means lacking the power to do something
comfort is consolation, compensation for loss

explanation.surface: Someone awkward because they cannot get any redress.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncomfortable means ill at ease, awkward, embarrassed.

clue.text: Changing notes, head of department for handler

indicators.note: changing notes means one musical note letter, F, is swapped for another, C

parts.note: a professor heads a university department

explanation.surface: A professor changes his lecture notes for a departmental head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' here are musical note letters: F becomes C.
explanation.definitionFit: A processor is something that handles or treats material or data.

clue.text: Society unwilling to convey animal from India

parts.note: loth, also spelt loath, means reluctant
to bear is to carry or convey

explanation.surface: A society refusing to transport an Indian animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloth bear is a shaggy insect-eating bear of India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Listen to utter gossip

parts.note: to hear is to listen
to say is to utter

explanation.surface: Listening to complete tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' reads as an adjective, complete, but is the verb to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is rumour, information passed on by word of mouth.

clue.text: Eccentric on trial, very foolish person

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a nut is an eccentric or crazy person
a case is a trial in court

explanation.surface: An eccentric defendant on trial behaving very foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is slang for a mad or foolish person.

clue.text: Tops of Italian mountains behind us, extremely steep

indicators.note: tops of means the first letter of each of the following five words is taken

explanation.surface: Peaks of Italian mountains rising behind us, extremely steep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tops of' seems to apply only to 'Italian mountains' but takes the first letter of all five words through 'extremely'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to soak or saturate, to steep something in a liquid or influence.

clue.text: Wading bird, for instance, on back of boat

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
re means on, concerning

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of boat

explanation.surface: A wading bird, perhaps, perched on the stern of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like wading bird.
